summary: Work that keeps running with no end date, such as a service you provide every day.
example: Collection Service, which moves produce from every depot to the buyer, every day of the season.
definition: An operation is work that keeps running with no end date: a service your organisation provides every day, one it is setting up (planned), or one it has stopped (retired). Work that ends is a project or a programme. An operation is named for the service; a project that sets it up or changes it is named for that change and hands it over when done. It has a service owner, the role responsible for it, and a team that runs it. KPIs show how well it runs. An operation can be part of a programme. An operation is not a project (it does not end), not a team (the team runs it), and not a data source (where records are kept). Its checks are advice and never stop you saving.

cues.operation: a service or routine that runs every day, week or month

/metadata/name.guide: The name people use for the service.

poor.why: Names a change with an end. That is a project, not the service.
Names the team that runs the service, not the service.

/spec/purpose.guide: What the service does and what for. No end date and no target figure.
good: Check every delivery for quality and route failures into rework.
Move produce from every depot to the buyer within a day of intake.
Keep one record per member, current enough to pay, count and contact them from.

poor.text: Introduce quality checks at every depot by the end of 2026.
poor.why: Work with an end. Introducing the checks is a project.
A target, not what the service does: the figure belongs to an indicator.
A topic, not a service: say what it does and for whom.

/spec/status.guide: Planned: being set up, not yet in use. Running: in use today. Retired: no longer offered.

/spec/serviceOwner.guide: The role responsible for the whole service. It takes over the service from the project that sets it up. A role, not a person. If none fits, add the role first.

poor.why: A person, not a role. Pick the role the person has.

/spec/team.guide: The team that runs the service. If none fits, add the team first.

/spec/serviceWindow.guide: When the service runs: which days and hours.
good: Daily through the season, reduced rounds out of season.

poor.why: Nobody can plan around it: say when the service runs.
Dates with an end describe a project; an operation keeps running.

/spec/funding.guide: The budgets that pay to run the service, and what it costs each month or year. Add one line per currency and period.
good: Refresher training, monitoring and the annual list review, 85,000 a year from the operating budget, requested

poor.text: The project's last funding line, kept open after it closes
poor.why: Project money stops when the project closes. Record the service's running costs on the service.

poor.text: A line with no amount, for a cost nobody has worked out yet
poor.why: Each line needs an amount. If the cost is unknown, add it as an issue under the project's risks.

/spec/funding/-/amount.guide: What running the service costs for one period, in the line's currency.

/spec/funding/-/per.guide: The period the amount is for: month or year.

/spec/funding/-/source.guide: The budget that pays this line. If there is none yet, leave it empty and set the status to requested or unfunded.

/spec/funding/-/status.guide: Whether the money is approved, requested or unfunded.

/spec/programmes.guide: The programmes this service is part of, if any.

poor.text: market-access-programme, because the same team works on it
poor.why: Sharing a team does not make it part of the programme. Pick a programme only if this service works towards its change.

/spec/kpis.guide: The KPIs that show whether the service runs as well as it should. If none fits, add the KPI first.

poor.why: Measures a wider result. Pick a KPI that shows how the service itself performs.

/spec/data.guide: The data the service reads, and the data it creates and where it goes.

/spec/data/consumes/-/source.guide: A data source the service reads but does not change.

/spec/data/consumes/-/purpose.guide: What the service uses the data for, in one sentence.
good: Identify members with deliveries due for a check this season.

poor.why: Says what the data is, not what the service does with it.

/spec/data/consumes/-/handoff.guide: How the data reaches the service: a feed, a file transfer, a shared database, manual re-entry or paper.

/spec/data/consumes/-/personalData.guide: Whether the data includes personal data, sensitive personal data, or none.

/spec/data/produces/-/output.guide: What the service creates: records in an existing source, documents or files, an extract or report, or a new data source.

/spec/data/produces/-/sink.guide: Where the data the service creates is kept.

/spec/data/produces/-/purpose.guide: What the produced data is for, in one sentence.
good: Record quality check results for each delivery.

poor.why: Says nothing about what is recorded or why.

/spec/data/produces/-/refresh.guide: How often this data is updated.

/spec/data/produces/-/personalData.guide: Whether the data includes personal data, sensitive personal data, or none.

/spec/mandate.guide: What allows or requires the service, such as a decision, policy, law, contract or request.

/spec/mandate/-/title.guide: The title of the decision or document, as it is written.

poor.why: Name the decision or policy that requires the service, or leave this empty.

/spec/mandate/-/issuer.guide: The board, committee or role in Cartograph that issued it. If it is not there yet, add it first.
good: Sponsor, one of this work's roles

poor.why: Pick the body from the list instead of typing it.

/spec/mandate/-/issuedBy.guide: The outside body that issued it, such as a government, regulator or funder.

/spec/notes.guide: Anything else people should know about this service.

Project:/spec/operation.ask: Which project sets this service up, or changes it?
Project:/spec/operation.ifNone: For a planned service, add the project that sets it up and choose this service on it. A running service needs none until it has to change.

checks.service-purpose: Say what the service does, day in and day out.
checks.service-owner: Name the role responsible for the service.
checks.service-hours: Give the hours and days the service runs.
checks.alignment-programmes: Pick a programme only if the service is part of it.
checks.measures-kpis: Name at least one KPI that shows how well the service runs.
checks.service-status: Once the project that sets up this service is done, mark the service running.
